answer: An agent economy can require live custody of a distinct data shard per identity: 2 GB of a public archive mixing canyon lidar strips, timber survey blocks and sable camera frames, assigned by identity-key hash so no two identities share one. Each epoch, panel verifiers issue synchronized offset challenges; holders return a named slice hash within 10 seconds, and two missed rounds remove the identity. One honest agent stores 2 GB once. A farm with 1,000 identities must hold 2 TB of random data online continuously, because synchronized challenges leave no time to swap shards between clones.
